quickAnswerTitle: Quick Answer: Comfort Colors 1717 vs Gildan 5000
quickAnswer: Choose Comfort Colors 1717 if you want a heavier 6.1 oz/yd² ring-spun cotton tee with a garment-dyed look and relaxed fit. Choose Gildan 5000 if you want a 5.3 oz/yd² Heavy Cotton tee that is commonly used for everyday wear and custom printing. Check the colour-specific fibre content, size chart and current price: the fabric composition is not identical across every colour.
intro: Comfort Colors 1717 and Gildan 5000 are two widely used blank T-shirts, but they target different preferences. The 1717 is a heavier garment-dyed ring-spun cotton tee with a relaxed fit. The Gildan 5000 is a lighter Heavy Cotton style with a classic fit. This is a specification-based comparison using the manufacturers' published product information, not a personal wear or wash test.

sections.heading: At a glance: weight, fabric and fit
paragraphs: Comfort Colors lists the 1717 at 6.1 oz/yd² and 100% ring-spun US cotton. Its product information describes a garment-dyed fabric and relaxed fit. Gildan lists the 5000 at 5.3 oz/yd² and 100% US cotton for the standard solid-colour version, with a classic fit. Some heather and special colours use fibre blends, so always check the composition for the colour you are ordering.

sections.heading: Fabric weight and hand feel
paragraphs: The 1717 is 0.8 oz/yd² heavier than the Gildan 5000. That difference is useful when choosing a garment, but weight alone does not prove that one shirt is softer, more durable or better made. Yarn type, knitting, dyeing, finishing and personal preference all affect how a tee feels.

Ring-spun cotton is made by twisting and thinning fibres into yarn; Gildan's 5000 product page identifies its own fabric as Heavy Cotton. If you prefer a heavier tee, the 1717 is the more obvious specification match. If you want a lighter-weight blank, the Gildan 5000 may suit you better.

sections.heading: Garment dye versus the Gildan 5000 finish
paragraphs: Comfort Colors describes the 1717 as garment-dyed. The garment is dyed after it has been constructed, which gives the product its characteristic washed colour appearance. The manufacturer says its garments are pre-shrunk during garment-dye and wash processes and describes pigment-dyed colours as having a vintage look.

Do not assume every colour behaves identically: Comfort Colors distinguishes pigment-dye and reactive-dye colours. Gildan 5000 is sold in a wide range of colours and its colour-specific fibre composition can vary. The official product pages are the best place to confirm the exact option.

sections.heading: Fit and sizing: relaxed versus classic
paragraphs: Comfort Colors describes the 1717 as a relaxed-fit tubular-body tee. Gildan describes the 5000 as a classic-fit shirt. These labels are not standardized measurements, so do not assume that the same tagged size will produce the same shoulder width, chest room or body length.

Compare the size charts before buying. Measure a T-shirt you already like while it is laid flat, then compare its chest width and body length with the manufacturer's chart. If you are ordering for a group or a print run, consider ordering a sample in the intended colour and size before placing a bulk order.

sections.heading: Which one makes more sense for printing or merchandise?
paragraphs: Both models are used as blank garments, but the best choice depends on the artwork, audience and budget. The Gildan 5000 is positioned as a versatile Heavy Cotton tee and is listed for common decoration methods such as screen printing and embroidery. Comfort Colors' heavier garment-dyed surface creates a different visual style that may suit vintage-inspired merchandise.

Before committing to a print run, ask the printer whether the ink, transfer or embroidery method is suitable for the chosen fabric and dye. Garment-dyed colour variation can be part of the desired look, but it may not be right when a highly uniform colour match is essential.

sections.heading: Washing and shrinkage: avoid blanket promises
paragraphs: Comfort Colors says the 1717 is pre-shrunk during garment dye and wash processes and describes it as having almost no shrinkage at home. That is the manufacturer's claim, not a guarantee that every wearer will see zero dimensional change under every laundry condition.

Follow the care label on either shirt. Washing temperature, dryer heat and repeated laundering can affect cotton garments. We have not independently washed or measured these two models, so we do not assign a measured shrinkage percentage or claim that one will last longer.

sections.heading: Which T-shirt should you choose?
paragraphs: Choose Comfort Colors 1717 if you specifically want a heavier ring-spun cotton tee, a relaxed fit and the muted garment-dyed aesthetic. It is the clearer match for a vintage-inspired casual look, provided the colour and price work for your project.

Choose Gildan 5000 if you prefer a 5.3 oz/yd² classic-fit blank, want to compare a broad colour range, or need a practical option for custom printing. Check the fibre blend of the exact colour before ordering, especially for heather shades.

Before buying, compare four details on the current listings: fabric weight, fibre composition for the chosen colour, garment measurements and return terms. For a bulk order, get a sample first; product specifications cannot tell you exactly how a garment will feel or fit on your body.

faqs.question: Which is heavier, Comfort Colors 1717 or Gildan 5000?
faqs.answer: Comfort Colors lists the 1717 at 6.1 oz/yd², while Gildan lists the 5000 at 5.3 oz/yd². The 1717 is heavier by the manufacturers' published specifications.

faqs.question: Is Comfort Colors 1717 100% cotton?
faqs.answer: Comfort Colors lists the 1717 as 100% ring-spun US cotton. Check the exact product and colour listing in case a special variant has different details.

faqs.question: Is Gildan 5000 always 100% cotton?
faqs.answer: The standard solid-colour Gildan 5000 is listed as 100% US cotton, but the manufacturer lists fibre blends for some heather and special colours. Check the chosen colour's composition.

faqs.question: Which shirt is better for screen printing?
faqs.answer: Both are used as blank T-shirts. Gildan positions the 5000 as a versatile decoration blank, while Comfort Colors offers a heavier garment-dyed look. Ask your printer to confirm the best process for the exact fabric and colour.

faqs.question: Does Comfort Colors 1717 shrink?
faqs.answer: Comfort Colors says its garments are pre-shrunk during garment dye and wash processes and describes them as having almost no shrinkage at home. Follow the care label; this is not a guarantee of zero change in every laundry condition.
